title: Model-facing knowledge_update rewrites durable curated knowledge without user-bound authorization

affectedLocations.label: entrypoint
affectedLocations.detail: Registers knowledge_update as a model-facing tool.

affectedLocations.label: root_control
affectedLocations.detail: Guard allows destructive model tools unless config is explicitly false.

affectedLocations.label: sink
affectedLocations.detail: Writes LLM-produced knowledge body to a temp file.

attackerControlledSource: Untrusted chat/retrieved/stored content can influence model tool selection; pending memory text and optional model-supplied note are then embedded in the curator prompt.
sinkOrBrokenControl: The operation is gated only by an opt-out flag defaulting to allow and feature configuration. It does not invoke isAuthorized, createConfirmation, or validateConfirmation before rewriting KNOWLEDGE.md.
impact: Prompt injection or model error can prematurely promote attacker-influenced memories into durable curated context, rewrite the knowledge body, and shape future agent behavior.
plausibility: The registered tool reads pending memories, sends existing and new content to an LLM, and atomically replaces KNOWLEDGE.md. No user-bound authorization is present on this path.
closestControl: Pending-memory filtering, promotion caps, LLM instructions, and atomic write protect consistency but do not authenticate the requested state change or constrain semantic prompt injection.

candidateLocalValidation.method: static source-to-sink trace and configuration-default verification
candidateLocalValidation.counterevidence: Requires Schicht 1.5 plus an LLM configuration, is per-workspace/agent, uses pending items, and writes atomically; these are preconditions/impact bounds, not authorization.

candidateLocalAttackPath.source: untrusted content influencing model and/or pending memory text
transformations: pending memories and note enter curator prompt
candidateLocalAttackPath.outcome: persistent curated knowledge/agent context is modified
